graders.name: blocking-questions
graders.evidence:
The design docs for the export feature are written, with no code and nothing committed. Every cross-link between them resolves.

The design in brief:

- **PDF download:** rendered on demand from current trip data and never stored.
- **Email to self:** sent synchronously in the request, with no queue, only to the account's own verified email. The endpoint accepts no recipient field at all, so it can't be used to mail anyone else.
- **One new table, `itinerary_exports`:** one row per export attempt, which serves as the audit log, rate-limit ledger and idempotency record.
- **Five invariants**, each enforced in app code and by a Postgres constraint: ownership, recipient, rate limit, one email per click, and consistent outcome records.
- **Four phases:** foundations, PDF download, email, hardening.

One trade-off is accepted in the design: if the server dies between the provider accepting the email and the row being updated, a retry can send a duplicate.

## Questions that block work

1. **Auth and trip tables:** are they built in this repo as part of this work, or arriving from another workstream? I assumed this workstream builds the minimum (users, trips, itinerary items) in Phase 0.
2. **Hosting:** Vercel serverless or a long-lived Node server, and what is the request timeout? I assumed Vercel on the Node runtime; this decides whether synchronous render-and-send holds up.
3. **Email:** is a provider and verified sending domain already in place? I assumed Resend, set up in Phase 2.

## Decisions to confirm

These are my choices, marked `(proposed)` in the docs:

- **Stack:** Drizzle, Auth.js, zod, Vitest, pnpm, `@react-pdf/renderer`, Resend.
- **Rate limits:** 5 emails and 30 downloads per user per clock hour; failed attempts count.
- **Empty itinerary:** refused with `422` rather than exported as a blank PDF.
- **Attachment cap:** 10 MB; the provider's actual limit is unverified.
- **Stuck exports:** a `pending` row older than 2 minutes is treated as failed.
- **Retention:** export rows pruned after 30 days.
- **Bounce handling:** none in v1.
- **Response shapes:** the HTTP status codes, error codes and error body format.
- **Commit rule:** `CLAUDE.md` carries the architect skill's "no AI co-author trailer" rule, which overrides the default attribution for this repo. Say so if you'd rather keep the trailer.

The first unblocked tasks are P0-1 (scaffold) and P0-2 (database and migrations); the auth and trip-table tasks wait on question 1.

Files are in the repo root:
- SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md
- ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md
- TODO_WORKFLOW.md
- CLAUDE.md
- docs/handoff.md

graders.evidence:
# Itinerary Export — Architecture & Roadmap

Version: 0.1 · Status: Draft, awaiting confirmation of `(proposed)` items · Owner: TBD · Date: 2026-11-11

Related: [SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md) (apex) · [TODO_WORKFLOW.md](TODO_WORKFLOW.md) · [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) · [docs/handoff.md](docs/handoff.md)

Derived from the SoT. Scope, invariants (I1–I5), decisions (D1–D7) and open
questions (Q1–Q9) are defined there and only referenced here. This is a
single-feature doc set, so there is no modular `docs/architecture/` split; create
one if this file outgrows a single read.

## 0. Executive context

Users of the trip-planning app want their itinerary as a PDF, and want it sent
to their own inbox. The feature is two endpoints on top of one new table. The
PDF is rendered on demand and never stored; the email is sent synchronously to
the account's verified address and nowhere else. The repo is empty, so Phase 0
covers the minimum app foundations the feature stands on.

## 1. Tech stack

Next.js and Postgres are given. Everything else is `(proposed)` until confirmed
(SoT [Q1–Q5](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions)). Versions are pinned at
scaffold time (task P0-1) and recorded in this table.

| Layer | Tech | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Web framework | Next.js, App Router, TypeScript | UI and route handlers |
| Database | Postgres | System of record; second enforcement boundary for I1–I5 |
| ORM / migrations | Drizzle + drizzle-kit `(proposed)` | Schema, SQL migrations |
| Auth | Auth.js `(proposed)` | Session → `{ id, email, emailVerifiedAt }` |
| Validation | zod `(proposed)` | Strict request schemas (I2) |
| PDF | `@react-pdf/renderer` `(proposed)`, Node runtime | Itinerary → PDF buffer (D3) |
| Email | Resend `(proposed)` behind `mailer.ts` | Send with attachment (D7) |
| Tests | Vitest `(proposed)` + a real Postgres for constraint tests | Unit + integration |
| Package manager | pnpm `(proposed)` | — |

## 2. Data schema

ID type is shown as `uuid`; if the core tables use something else, `itinerary_exports` follows them.

### 2.1 Prerequisite tables (minimum this feature needs)

Owned by the core app (SoT [Q1](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions)). Extra columns are fine; these must exist.

**`users`**

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | PK |
| `email` | `text` | `NOT NULL`, unique (case-insensitive) |
| `email_verified_at` | `timestamptz` | nullable; `NULL` = unverified |

**`trips`**

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | PK |
| `owner_id` | `uuid` | `NOT NULL`, FK → `users(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `title` | `text` | `NOT NULL`, non-empty |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | `date` | `NOT NULL`, `CHECK (end_date >= start_date)` |
| `timezone` | `text` | `NOT NULL`, IANA name; all itinerary times render in this zone |

> `UNIQUE (id, owner_id)` on `trips` is required. It is the target of the
> composite FK that enforces I1 at the DB. Do not drop it as "redundant with the PK".

**`itinerary_items`**

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | PK |
| `trip_id` | `uuid` | `NOT NULL`, FK → `trips(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `starts_at` | `timestamptz` | `NOT NULL` |
| `ends_at` | `timestamptz` | nullable, `CHECK (ends_at IS NULL OR ends_at >= starts_at)` |
| `title` | `text` | `NOT NULL`, non-empty |
| `location`, `notes` | `text` | nullable |
| `position` | `integer` | `NOT NULL`; tie-break within the same `starts_at` |

Index: `(trip_id, starts_at, position)` — the export read path.

### 2.2 `itinerary_exports` (owned by this feature)

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` |
| `trip_id` | `uuid` | `NOT NULL` |
| `user_id` | `uuid` | `NOT NULL` |
| `channel` | `text` | `NOT NULL`, `CHECK (channel IN ('download','email'))` |
| `status` | `text` | `NOT NULL` default `'pending'`, `CHECK (status IN ('pending','succeeded','failed'))` |
| `idempotency_key` | `uuid` | nullable |
| `window_start` | `timestamptz` | `NOT NULL`; `date_trunc('hour', created_at)` |
| `slot` | `smallint` | `NOT NULL` |
| `error_code` | `text` | nullable; one of the codes in [§3.3](#33-failure-paths) |
| `provider_message_id` | `text` | nullable; email channel only |
| `pdf_bytes` | `integer` | nullable; size of the rendered PDF |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | `NOT NULL` default `now()` |
| `completed_at` | `timestamptz` | nullable |

Table constraints:

| Constraint | Enforces |
|---|---|
| `FOREIGN KEY (trip_id, user_id) REFERENCES trips (id, owner_id) ON DELETE CASCADE` | I1 |
| No recipient column exists | I2 |
| `UNIQUE (user_id, channel, window_start, slot)` | I3 |
| `CHECK ((channel = 'email' AND slot BETWEEN 1 AND 5) OR (channel = 'download' AND slot BETWEEN 1 AND 30))` | I3 — literals must match the limits in SoT I3 |
| `UNIQUE (user_id, idempotency_key)` | I4 |
| `CHECK ((channel = 'email') = (idempotency_key IS NOT NULL))` | I4 |
| `CHECK ((status = 'failed') = (error_code IS NOT NULL))` | I5 |
| `CHECK ((status = 'pending') = (completed_at IS NULL))` | I5 |

Indexes: the two unique constraints, plus `(trip_id)` for the cascade.

Decision call-outs:

- Changing a rate limit means changing SoT I3 **and** the slot `CHECK` in one migration. The number has one definition (SoT) and one mirror (the constraint).
- No `sending` status. Sending is synchronous (D2); a `pending` row older than 2 minutes `(proposed)` is treated as `failed / unknown_outcome` when read. If D2 is reversed and a worker is added, a claim state is introduced then.
- Failed attempts keep their slot (SoT I3), which also stops a client hammering a failing provider.

## 3. Backend

### 3.1 Structure

Paths are `(proposed)`; they become fact when P0-1 lands.

| Module | Responsibility | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/api/trips/[tripId]/export/pdf/route.ts` | HTTP for download: session, call service, stream PDF | Maps service errors to [§3.3](#33-failure-paths) responses |
| `src/app/api/trips/[tripId]/export/email/route.ts` | HTTP for email: session, strict schema, `Idempotency-Key` | Same |
| `src/server/export/service.ts` | The only orchestrator: ownership check → rate limit + reserve row → load snapshot → render → (send) → finalize row | Any throw after the row exists finalizes it as `failed` with a code; never leaves a row `pending` on a handled error |
| `src/server/export/reserve.ts` | Idempotency lookup, window count, slot insert (pseudocode below) | Constraint violations become typed errors, not 500s |
| `src/server/export/snapshot.ts` | One query: trip + ordered items → plain `ItinerarySnapshot` | Trip not found / not owned → `not_found` |
| `src/server/export/render.ts` | Pure function `ItinerarySnapshot → Buffer`. No DB, no network | Throws `render_failed`; enforces the size cap → `pdf_too_large` |
| `src/server/export/mailer.ts` | `sendItineraryEmail({ to, subject, pdf, filename, idempotencyKey })` via the provider | Timeout 10 s `(proposed)`; any non-success → `email_send_failed`. No internal retry (the user retries; I3 bounds it) |

Reserve step (pseudocode):

```
if channel = email:
    existing = SELECT … WHERE user_id = :u AND idempotency_key = :k
    if existing: return replay(existing)            -- I4, see §3.3 for replay rules
w = date_trunc('hour', now())
n = SELECT count(*) WHERE user_id = :u AND channel = :c AND window_start = :w
if n >= limit(c): raise rate_limited                -- I3, app boundary
INSERT … (slot = n + 1, window_start = w, status = 'pending')
    FK violation (trip_id, user_id)        → not_found        -- I1, DB boundary
    unique violation on idempotency_key    → re-read row, replay
    unique violation on slot               → a concurrent request took it: recount and retry once
    CHECK violation on slot range          → rate_limited     -- I3, DB boundary
```

Recipient lookup for email (I2), done by the service immediately before sending:

```
SELECT u.email FROM itinerary_exports e JOIN users u ON u.id = e.user_id
WHERE e.id = :exportId AND e.status = 'pending' AND u.email_verified_at IS NOT NULL
no row → email_unverified
```

Finalize (I5): `UPDATE itinerary_exports SET status = …, completed_at = now(), … WHERE id = :id AND status = 'pending'`.

Output hygiene: the download filename is a slug of the trip title restricted to
`[a-z0-9-]` (fallback `trip`) plus `-itinerary.pdf`; CR/LF are stripped from the
email subject. Both exist to prevent header injection from user-authored titles.

### 3.2 API contract

Both routes require a session. Error body: `{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string } }` `(proposed)`.

| Method & path | Request | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/trips/:tripId/export/pdf` | — | `200`, `Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<slug>-itinerary.pdf"`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` | `401`, `404`, `422`, `429`, `500` |
| `POST /api/trips/:tripId/export/email` | Header `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` (required). Body: empty object; unknown keys rejected | `200 { "exportId": uuid, "status": "succeeded", "sentTo": "<masked email>" }` | `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `429`, `500`, `502` |

The download is a `GET` that writes one audit row (D5). It must be triggered by a
plain `<a>` and never prefetched.

### 3.3 Failure paths

Status codes and error codes are `(proposed)`.

| Component | What fails | Row outcome | Response | What the user can do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Route | No session | no row | `401 unauthenticated` | Sign in |
| Email route | Missing/invalid `Idempotency-Key`, or unknown body keys | no row | `400 invalid_request` | Client bug; not user-recoverable |
| Service / FK | Trip missing or not owned (I1) | no row | `404 not_found` | — |
| Service | Email not verified (I2) | no row if caught by the app check; else `failed / email_unverified` | `403 email_unverified` | Verify email, retry |
| Reserve | Rate limit hit (I3) | no row | `429 rate_limited` + `Retry-After` (seconds to next window) | Wait |
| Reserve | Same key, earlier row `succeeded` (I4) | unchanged | `200`, same body as the original | Nothing; it was sent once |
| Reserve | Same key, earlier row `failed` | unchanged | The original error, replayed | Click again (new key) |
| Reserve | Same key, earlier row `pending` and under 2 min old | unchanged | `409 export_in_progress` | Wait |
| Reserve | Same key, earlier row `pending` and over 2 min old | read as `failed / unknown_outcome` | `502 email_send_failed` | Click again; may produce a duplicate (D4) |
| Snapshot | Trip has no items (Q6) | `failed / empty_itinerary` | `422 empty_itinerary` | Add items |
| Render | Library throws | `failed / render_failed` | `500 render_failed` | Retry; logged with `exportId` |
| Render | PDF over the size cap (Q9) | `failed / pdf_too_large` | `422 pdf_too_large` | — (should not occur for text-only itineraries) |
| Mailer | Provider error or timeout | `failed / email_send_failed` | `502 email_send_failed` | Click again |
| Finalize | DB write fails after the provider accepted | stays `pending` → later `unknown_outcome` | `500` | Email probably arrived; a retry may duplicate (D4) |
| DB | Unavailable at any step | none or `pending` | `500` | Retry |

## 4. Frontend

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Trip page → **Export** menu | Two actions: *Download PDF*, *Email to me* |
| Download PDF | Plain `<a href="/api/trips/:id/export/pdf">`. Not a Next `<Link>` (no prefetch; see §3.2) |
| Email to me | Button → `POST` with a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` key per click. Disabled while the request is in flight. An automatic network retry reuses the same key; a new click makes a new one |
| Success | Toast: "Sent to a•••@example.com" using `sentTo`, so the user knows which inbox to check |
| Errors | Mapped by `error.code`: `email_unverified` → link to verification; `rate_limited` → "Try again in N minutes" from `Retry-After`; `empty_itinerary` → "Add something to your itinerary first"; everything else → generic retry message |
| No email input field | By design (I2) |

PDF layout: trip title and date range; one section per day in the trip's

graders.name: blocking-questions
graders.evidence:
The design docs are written and cross-linked; no code is written and nothing is committed. Three questions block the first build tasks, and the library choices are unverified because the package registry was unreachable from here.

## The design in brief

- **Flow:** the user clicks "Email me a PDF" on a trip, the server queues an export, renders the PDF, and emails it as an attachment. The button polls for a status of sent or failed.
- **Recipient:** always the signed-in user's own verified account email. No request can name a recipient, so the feature can't be used to mail other people.
- **Queue:** the export row in Postgres is the job, so there is no Redis or separate queue. A cron sweep recovers anything missed or stuck.
- **PDF:** rendered on the server, text only, held in memory and never stored.
- **Failures:** transient email errors retry with backoff up to three attempts; permanent ones fail with a code the UI turns into a message.
- **Order of work:** foundation, trip and itinerary tables, PDF renderer, export pipeline, UI, hardening. Each phase ships on its own.

## Questions that block Phase 0/1

1. **Hosting:** serverless (e.g. Vercel) or a long-lived Node server? This decides how the job is triggered and how often the cron sweep can run. Until you answer, the design stays serverless-compatible.
2. **Auth:** which auth system, and does it guarantee a verified email? I assumed Auth.js with a verified-email timestamp on `users`.
3. **Itinerary model:** is there an existing schema to match, or do I start from the minimal `trips` / `itinerary_items` model I sketched?

## Decisions to confirm

These are my choices, marked `(proposed)` in the docs:

- **Libraries:** `@react-pdf/renderer` for the PDF, Resend for email, Drizzle for the ORM, zod, Vitest and Playwright, pnpm.
- **Job trigger:** Next.js `after()` plus a cron sweep, rather than a dedicated worker process.
- **Email only:** no direct PDF download in v1; adding one later is a single task.
- **Owner only:** collaborators on a shared trip cannot export it.
- **Limits:** 10 exports per user per 24 hours, 3 send attempts, 10 MB PDF cap, 5-minute stuck-job timeout.
- **Status codes:** 202 for a new export, 200 when one is already in progress, 404 for both "missing" and "not yours", 409 for unverified email, 422 for an empty itinerary, 429 for rate limit.
- **Times:** itinerary dates and times are stored as local wall-clock values with no time zone, and printed as entered.
- **"Sent" means the provider accepted the message:** bounces are not tracked.
- **Duplicate emails:** preventing one after a crash relies on the email provider supporting idempotency keys, which I have not confirmed for Resend. Without it, one duplicate is possible in that case.
- **PDF format:** A4, English, one unbranded template.

`CLAUDE.md` carries the template's git rules, including feature branches only and no AI co-author trailer on commits. Its commands table is empty until the scaffold exists. The git root is one level above this directory, so check that is intended before the first commit.

# Architecture & Roadmap — Itinerary PDF Export & Email

**Version:** 0.1 · **Status:** Draft, no code written · **Owner:** repo owner · **Updated:** 2026-11-11

Derived from [SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md) (wins on conflict) · Tasks: [TODO_WORKFLOW.md](TODO_WORKFLOW.md) · Rules: [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) · Log: [docs/handoff.md](docs/handoff.md)

`I#`, `D#`, `OQ-#` refer to [invariants](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#3-invariants), [decisions](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#4-decisions) and [open questions](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions) in the SoT. `(proposed)` marks a choice not yet confirmed.

## 0. Executive context

The repo is empty. The feature is small, but it is the first thing built, so
Phases 0–1 lay the minimum foundation it needs (app scaffold, database, auth,
the trip and itinerary tables) and nothing more. The feature itself is three
pieces: a pure PDF renderer, a Postgres-backed job that renders and emails, and
one button with a status line.

Library versions could not be checked from the authoring environment (no
package-registry access). Every library-specific API named below must be
verified against the pinned version in task T0.1 before it is relied on.

## 1. Tech stack

| Layer | Tech | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Web framework | Next.js, App Router, TypeScript (given) | Pages, route handlers, post-response job kick-off |
| Database | PostgreSQL (given) | Domain data and the export job queue (D1) |
| DB access / migrations | Drizzle ORM + SQL migrations `(proposed, OQ-8)` | Typed queries; migrations carry the constraints in §2 |
| Auth | Auth.js `(proposed, OQ-2)` | Session, user id, verified email |
| Validation | zod `(proposed)` | Strict request parsing (I1) |
| PDF | `@react-pdf/renderer` `(proposed, D3)` | Server-side render to a Buffer |
| Email | Resend `(proposed, D5, OQ-4)` behind `EmailSender` | Transactional send with attachment |
| Job trigger | Next.js `after()` + host cron hitting the sweep route `(proposed, D2, OQ-1)` | Run the job after the response; recover missed/stuck jobs |
| Tests | Vitest (unit/integration against real Postgres), Playwright (one e2e) `(proposed)` | See §6 |
| Package manager | pnpm `(proposed)` | — |

## 2. Data schema

Types are PostgreSQL. All ids are `uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`. All tables have `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`.

### 2.1 `users` (owned by auth, OQ-2)

Columns this feature depends on. The auth library's own columns are not listed.

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `email` | text | NOT NULL, UNIQUE |
| `email_verified_at` | timestamptz | NULL = unverified (I3) |

### 2.2 `trips` (minimal, OQ-3)

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `user_id` | uuid | NOT NULL, FK → `users(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| `title` | text | NOT NULL, `CHECK (char_length(title) BETWEEN 1 AND 200)` (I8) |
| `start_date` | date | NOT NULL |
| `end_date` | date | NOT NULL, `CHECK (end_date >= start_date)` |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL DEFAULT now() |

Indexes: `(user_id)`; **`UNIQUE (id, user_id)`** — redundant for uniqueness, required as the target of the composite FK that enforces I2.

### 2.3 `itinerary_items` (minimal, OQ-3)

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK |
| `trip_id` | uuid | NOT NULL, FK → `trips(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| `day_date` | date | NOT NULL (wall-clock, D7) |
| `start_time` | time | NULL (wall-clock, D7) |
| `end_time` | time | NULL, `CHECK (end_time IS NULL OR start_time IS NOT NULL)` |
| `title` | text | NOT NULL, `CHECK (char_length(title) BETWEEN 1 AND 200)` (I8) |
| `location` | text | NULL, `CHECK (char_length(location) <= 300)` (I8) |
| `notes` | text | NULL, `CHECK (char_length(notes) <= 5000)` (I8) |
| `position` | integer | NOT NULL — order within a day |

Index: `(trip_id, day_date, position)` — the renderer's read order.

> The length caps are `(proposed)`. They are part of I8; do not remove them without revisiting it.

### 2.4 `itinerary_exports`

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | PK; also the email idempotency key (I6) |
| `trip_id` | uuid | NOT NULL |
| `user_id` | uuid | NOT NULL, FK → `users(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE (I1) |
| `status` | text | NOT NULL DEFAULT `'pending'`, `CHECK (status IN ('pending','processing','sent','failed'))` (I5) |
| `attempts` | smallint | NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `CHECK (attempts BETWEEN 0 AND 3)` — upper bound = `EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` |
| `next_attempt_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL DEFAULT now() |
| `locked_at` | timestamptz | NULL; set on claim |
| `error_code` | text | NULL, `CHECK` against the set in §3.5 |
| `provider_message_id` | text | NULL; set on `sent` |
| `sent_at` | timestamptz | NULL |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL DEFAULT now() |

Table constraints:

| Constraint | Enforces |
|---|---|
| `FOREIGN KEY (trip_id, user_id) REFERENCES trips(id, user_id) ON DELETE CASCADE` | I2 |
| `CHECK ((status = 'sent') = (sent_at IS NOT NULL))` | I5 |
| `CHECK ((status = 'failed') = (error_code IS NOT NULL))` | I5 |
| `CHECK ((status = 'processing') = (locked_at IS NOT NULL))` | I5 |
| `UNIQUE INDEX … (trip_id) WHERE status IN ('pending','processing')` | I4 |
| `BEFORE INSERT` trigger `exports_require_verified_email` `(proposed)` | I3 |

Other indexes: `(user_id, created_at DESC)` (rate-limit count, I7); `(next_attempt_at) WHERE status = 'pending'` and `(locked_at) WHERE status = 'processing'` (sweep).

Decision call-outs:

- `status` and `error_code` are `text` + `CHECK`, not Postgres enums: adding a value is a one-line constraint swap.
- There is **no recipient column and no PDF column** (I1, D4).
- Deleting a trip or user cascades to its exports; a worker whose guarded update then matches zero rows simply stops (§3.6).

## 3. Backend

### 3.1 Structure `(proposed layout)`

```
src/
  app/api/trips/[tripId]/exports/route.ts              POST   request an export
  app/api/trips/[tripId]/exports/[exportId]/route.ts   GET    poll status
  app/api/internal/exports/sweep/route.ts              POST   cron entry point
  server/db/                 schema + migrations (§2)
  server/exports/service.ts  requestExport(), getExport()
  server/exports/worker.ts   processExport(id), sweep()
  server/pdf/itinerary.tsx   renderItineraryPdf(data) -> Buffer   (pure, no I/O, D8)
  server/email/sender.ts     EmailSender interface, provider impl, in-memory fake
```

### 3.2 Services

| Unit | Responsibility | Must not |
|---|---|---|
| `requestExport(userId, tripId)` | In one transaction: per-user advisory lock → ownership (I2) → verified email (I3) → non-empty itinerary → rate limit (I7) → return active export or insert `pending` (I4). | Render, send, or accept a recipient. |
| `processExport(id)` | Claim → load → render → size check (I8) → send → mark terminal. Pseudocode in §3.3. | Run without a successful claim. |
| `sweep()` | Re-queue `processing` rows whose `locked_at` is older than `EXPORT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (or fail them with `worker_timeout` if attempts are exhausted); then run `processExport` for up to `SWEEP_BATCH` due `pending` rows. | Touch terminal rows. |
| `renderItineraryPdf(data)` | Pure function: trip + items → PDF Buffer. Groups by `day_date`, orders by `position`. User text is rendered as text, never as markup. | Query the DB, read env, or make network calls (D8). |
| `EmailSender.send(msg)` | Send one message with one attachment and an idempotency key; return `accepted(messageId)`, `rejected` (permanent) or `unavailable` (transient). | Throw for expected provider failures; decide retries. |

### 3.3 Job flow (pseudocode)

```
processExport(id):
  job = UPDATE itinerary_exports
           SET status='processing', locked_at=now(), attempts=attempts+1
         WHERE id=:id AND status='pending' AND next_attempt_at<=now()
        RETURNING *
  if no row: return                                  # not due, or another worker has it (I6)

  data = load trip + items + user in ONE consistent read
  if user.email_verified_at is null: fail('email_unverified')        # I3 re-check
  if data.items is empty:            fail('empty_itinerary')

  pdf = renderItineraryPdf(data)     # throws -> fail('render_failed')
  if pdf.length > PDF_MAX_BYTES:     fail('pdf_too_large')           # I8

  result = emailSender.send(to=user.email, attachment=pdf, idempotencyKey=job.id)
    accepted    -> status='sent', sent_at=now(), provider_message_id, locked_at=null
    rejected    -> fail('email_rejected')
    unavailable -> if job.attempts < EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                     status='pending', locked_at=null, next_attempt_at=now()+backoff(job.attempts)
                   else fail('email_send_failed')

every write above is guarded: … WHERE id=:id AND status='processing'   (I5)
fail(code): status='failed', error_code=code, locked_at=null
```

Kick-off: the `POST` handler schedules `processExport(id)` to run after the response is sent. If that never runs, the sweep finds the row.

### 3.4 Tunables

Single home for every number. All values `(proposed, OQ-7)`.

| Name | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPORT_RATE_LIMIT` | 10 new exports per user per rolling 24 h | I7 |
| `EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | 3 | retry, `attempts` CHECK |
| Backoff after attempt 1 / 2 | 1 min / 5 min | retry |
| `EXPORT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 5 min | sweep |
| `SWEEP_BATCH` | 10 | sweep |
| Sweep interval | 1 min, or the shortest the host's cron allows (OQ-1) | sweep |
| `PDF_MAX_BYTES` | 10 MB; must be ≤ the provider's attachment limit (OQ-4) | I8 |
| Client poll | every 2 s, give up after 60 s | §4 |

### 3.5 API contract

All routes require a session unless noted. Response bodies are JSON. Status codes are `(proposed)`.

| Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/trips/:tripId/exports` — body must be empty or `{}`; unknown fields rejected (I1) | `202 { id, status: "pending" }` new export · `200 { id, status }` an active export already existed (I4) | `400 invalid_body` · `401` · `403 bad_origin` · `404 not_found` (D9) · `409 email_unverified` (I3) · `422 empty_itinerary` · `429 rate_limited` + `Retry-After` (I7) · `503` DB unavailable |
| `GET /api/trips/:tripId/exports/:exportId` | `200 { id, status, errorCode, createdAt, sentAt }` | `401` · `404 not_found` (not the caller's export, wrong trip, or absent) |
| `POST /api/internal/exports/sweep` — no session; `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, constant-time compare | `200 { requeued, processed }` | `401` |

`error_code` values (also the DB `CHECK` set): `email_unverified`, `empty_itinerary`, `render_failed`, `pdf_too_large`, `email_rejected`, `email_send_failed`, `worker_timeout`.

### 3.6 Failure paths

| Component | What fails | What happens next |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` handler | DB unreachable | `503`; nothing was enqueued; the user can click again. |
| `POST` handler | Two concurrent requests for one trip | One insert wins; the other hits the I4 unique index and returns the winner's row with `200`. |
| Kick-off | Post-response work never runs (deploy, crash, platform limit) | Row stays `pending`; the next sweep processes it. |
| Worker | Process dies mid-job | Row stays `processing`; after `EXPORT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the sweep re-queues it, or fails it with `worker_timeout` if attempts are exhausted. |
| Worker | Dies after the provider accepted, before `sent` was written | Re-queued and re-sent with the same idempotency key; the provider de-duplicates (I6). If the provider cannot, one duplicate email is possible. |
| Worker | Trip or user deleted mid-job | Row is gone by cascade; the guarded update matches zero rows; the worker stops. No email if the delete landed before the load. |
| Worker | User's email changed or became unverified after the request | Recipient is resolved at send time: sends to the current verified address, or fails `email_unverified`. |
| Worker | Itinerary emptied after the request | `failed / empty_itinerary`. |
| Renderer | Throws | `failed / render_failed`, not retried (deterministic). Logged with export id, never with content. |
| Renderer | Output over `PDF_MAX_BYTES` | `failed / pdf_too_large`, not retried. |
| Email provider | Timeout, network error, 5xx, provider-side rate limit | Back to `pending` with backoff until `EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, then `failed / email_send_failed`. |
| Email provider | Permanent rejection (invalid or suppressed address, bad attachment) | `failed / email_rejected`, not retried. |
| Email provider | Accepts, then the message bounces later | Not detected; row stays `sent` (D6). |
| Sweep | Cron stops firing | New exports still run via kick-off; stuck/retrying rows wait. Alert on old non-terminal rows (§6). |
| Sweep | Two sweeps overlap | Safe: every claim is the same atomic guarded update. |

## 4. Frontend

One client component on the trip page: `ExportItineraryButton` ("Email me a PDF").

| UI state | Trigger | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| idle | initial; itinerary has items | Enabled button |
| disabled | itinerary has no items | Disabled button + hint (UX only; the server enforces it) |
| requesting | click | Button disabled, `aria-busy` |
| in progress | `202` or `200` from `POST` | "Preparing your PDF…"; polls `GET` per §3.4 |
| sent | poll returns `sent` | "Sent to your account email." |
| still working | poll window elapsed, not terminal | "Still working — it will arrive by email." Stops polling; not an error. |
| failed | poll returns `failed`, or `POST` errored | Message by code (below); "Try again" starts a **new** export |

| Code | User-facing message |
|---|---|
| `email_unverified` | Verify your email address first (link to verification). |
| `empty_itinerary` | Add something to the itinerary before exporting. |
| `rate_limited` | You've hit today's export limit. Try again later. |
| `pdf_too_large` | This itinerary is too large to email. |
| `email_rejected` | We couldn't deliver to your account email. Check the address in settings. |
| `render_failed`, `email_send_failed`, `worker_timeout`, `503`, network | Something went wrong on our side. Try again. |

Accessibility: status text lives in an `aria-live="polite"` region; the button is a real `<button>`; no state is conveyed by colour alone.

**Email** `(proposed)`: subject `Your itinerary: <trip title>` (CR/LF stripped); short text + HTML body; one attachment named `<ascii-slug-of-title>-itinerary.pdf`.

**PDF layout** `(proposed, OQ-9)`: A4 portrait; header with trip title and date range; one section per day in date order; each item shows time range (if any), title, location, notes; footer with page number and generation date. One bundled font with broad Unicode coverage, because user text will not be Latin-only — verify glyph coverage and fallback behaviour in T2.1.

## 5. Execution phases

Each phase ships on its own and leaves `main` working. Tasks: [TODO_WORKFLOW.md](TODO_WORKFLOW.md).

| Phase | Delivers | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **0 Foundation** | Scaffold, pinned versions, Postgres + migration tooling, auth, CI. Resolves OQ-1, OQ-2, OQ-8. | A signed-in page renders; CI runs lint, typecheck and tests against a real Postgres; `CLAUDE.md` commands table is filled with verified commands. |
| **1 Domain model** | `trips`, `itinerary_items` (§2.2–2.3), seed script. Resolves OQ-3. | Integration tests prove each `CHECK`/FK rejects bad rows. |
| **2 PDF renderer** | `renderItineraryPdf` + fixtures. No DB, no email. | Tests extract text from the PDF and assert day grouping, ordering, non-Latin text, empty optional fields. (Zero items never reaches the renderer; the service and worker reject it first.) |
| **3 Export pipeline** | `itinerary_exports` (§2.4), service, worker, `EmailSender` + fake, three routes. | Integration tests cover every row of §3.6 that does not need a real provider, and every invariant I1–I6 and I8 at **both** boundaries. |
| **4 UI** | `ExportItineraryButton`, states and messages in §4. | One Playwright run: click → fake sender receives one message with a PDF for the right user. |
| **5 Hardening** | Rate limit (I7), cron wiring, real provider, logging and alerts (§6). Resolves OQ-4, OQ-7. | A real email with a readable PDF arrives from a staging deploy; a killed worker is recovered by the sweep. |

## 6. Non-functional requirements

| Area | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Latency | `POST` returns without waiting on render or send. Target `(proposed)`: p95 under 30 s from click to provider acceptance. |
| Security | Session on every user route; `Origin` must match the app's host on `POST` (route handlers get no built-in CSRF check) `(proposed)`; sweep route protected by `CRON_SECRET`; ownership failures return 404 (D9); renderer does no network I/O (D8). |
| Privacy | PDF bytes, itinerary content and email addresses are never logged and never stored (D4). Logs carry ids only. |
| Secrets | `DATABASE_URL`, `EMAIL_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `CRON_SECRET`, auth secret — environment only, never committed. |
| Observability | One structured log line per status transition: `export_id`, `user_id`, `from`, `to`, `error_code`, `attempts`. Alert when any row is non-terminal for more than 15 min `(proposed)` or when the `failed` share spikes. |
| Testing | Unit: renderer, state machine. Integration (real Postgres): every DB constraint in §2 has a test that tries to violate it. E2E: one happy path with the fake sender. No test sends real email. |
| Deliverability | Sending domain needs SPF/DKIM/DMARC before Phase 5 goes live — a setup task for whoever owns DNS. |

# Source of Truth — Auth Service

Architecture and phases: [ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md) · Tasks: [TODO_WORKFLOW.md](TODO_WORKFLOW.md)

## Scope
Cloudflare Workers auth service (Hono + D1). Issues and validates session
tokens for POST /login, POST /logout, GET /session. Rate-limits POST /login
per client IP.

## Non-goals
- Per-account lockout or credential-stuffing defence. The per-IP limit is a
  flood limit; an attacker rotating IPs is not stopped by it.
- Rate limits on any endpoint other than POST /login. Password reset decides
  its own limits in its own task.

## Domain model
- `users` (D1): id, email, password_hash, created_at
- `sessions` (D1): id, user_id, token, expires_at
- Login rate-limit counters: not in D1. Held by the Workers Rate Limiting
  binding, keyed by client IP (see Decisions).

## Invariants
| # | Invariant | Enforced at |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Password hashes use scrypt, never stored plaintext | app layer (hash on write) + DB column has no plaintext default |
| 2 | A session token is single-use per refresh | app layer (rotate on use) + DB unique index on token |
| 3 | POST /login serves at most 100 requests per 60 s per client IP. Every request counts, successful or not. Excess requests get 429 before any credential work: no body parse, no D1 read, no scrypt. | app layer (Hono middleware on POST /login calling the Workers Rate Limiting binding, limit 100 / period 60 s) + Cloudflare WAF rate limiting rule on the zone for POST /login at the same threshold (proposed). Open: does the zone's plan allow a 60 s counting period? See roadmap §3.1 Q2. |

Invariant 3 is best-effort, not exact (proposed): binding counters are kept per
Cloudflare location and are eventually consistent, so a brief overshoot above
100 is possible.

## Decisions
- **Decision:** D1 over KV for sessions. **Why:** need a relational lookup by user_id for "log out everywhere". **Alternative rejected:** KV (no secondary index).

- **Decision:** client IP is read from `CF-Connecting-IP` only. **Why:** Cloudflare sets it; `X-Forwarded-For` is client-controlled and would let a caller pick their own bucket. **Alternative rejected:** `X-Forwarded-For`.

graders.name: declines-panel-result
graders.evidence:
**date-fns**, but first check whether you need either.

If all you're doing is formatting timestamps, the built-in `Intl` API covers it with zero dependencies:

```ts
new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }).format(date)
// "Nov 11, 2026, 3:42 PM"

new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat('en', { numeric: 'auto' }).format(-1, 'day')
// "yesterday"
```

If you want a library for custom format strings like `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, `formatDistanceToNow`, or date maths, I'd pick date-fns for a Next.js app:

- **Plain functions on native `Date`:** there is no wrapper object, so values pass cleanly between Server and Client Components.
- **Tree-shaking:** you ship only the functions you import. dayjs has a small core, but timezones, relative time and advanced formats each need a plugin registered with `dayjs.extend()`.
- **TypeScript:** each function is typed on its own, whereas dayjs plugin typings rely on module augmentation and can be finicky.

dayjs is the better choice if you prefer the chainable `dayjs(x).add(1, 'day').format()` style or are migrating from Moment.

Whichever you choose, formatting in the server's timezone or locale and then hydrating on the client in a different one causes hydration mismatches. Pass an explicit `timeZone` and locale, or format only on the client.

It's also a cheap decision to reverse: wrap the formatting in one `formatTimestamp()` helper and swapping later means changing one file.

# Ask the Council

A panel of advisors who are required to disagree, then a Chairman who
decides. Use for decisions and tradeoffs, not for gathering facts.

## Proactive use

If a decision is high-stakes and the options genuinely compete — architecture
choice, buy-vs-build, irreversible migration — invoke this without being
asked: announce in one line ("Convening the council: <decision>") and
proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill.

Gate it first: if you can't name what the wrong choice costs to reverse,
don't seat the council — decide directly and move on. A panel costs 4–6 opus
subagents; spend that only where being wrong is expensive to undo.

## Frame and seat the council

Restate the decision, the real options, and the binding constraints. If one
missing fact would flip the answer, ask it (max 1–2 questions) — otherwise
proceed on stated assumptions. Then spawn the advisors with the Agent tool,
all in one message, so they run in parallel. Each returns: **position · the
argument for the position · biggest risk they see · confidence (low/med/high)**. On `deep`,
once all seats report, show each advisor the others' positions
(unattributed) and have them name the single strongest opposing point.

## The seats (mandate + forbidden move = real divergence)

- **Pragmatic Executor** — what ships fastest and safest with current resources.
  *Forbidden:* greenfield / ideal-world answers.
- **First-Principles** — reason up from fundamentals and constraints.
  *Forbidden:* citing "best practice" or precedent.
- **The Contrarian** — argue against the front-runner.
  *Forbidden:* agreeing with the apparent consensus.
- **Long-term Architect** — model-first; what this is at 10× scale and in two
  years. *Forbidden:* optimizing for today only.
- **The Adversary** — how this breaks in prod: failure paths, data loss,
  security. *Forbidden:* assuming the happy path.
- **The Outsider** *(deep panel)* — an analogy from a different domain.
  *Forbidden:* the field's standard framing.

Default 4 = Executor, First-Principles, Long-term Architect, Adversary.
`deep` seats all 6 and adds the cross-critique round. The forbidden move is
what forces real divergence instead of four agents politely agreeing — keep
it non-negotiable; seat count never changes.

## Model routing

Spawn every advisor seat — and the deep-mode critique round — with the Agent
tool's `model` parameter set to `opus`: this is the one skill in the plugin
whose entire value is the quality of independent judgment per seat, and it
shouldn't silently inherit whatever subagent default a given session has.
The Chairman synthesis is never a subagent — it runs in the main thread, on
the session's own model, because committing to a recommendation needs the
full conversation context the advisors don't have. Naming `model: opus` in
the spawn itself is what makes this portable: it doesn't depend on any
installer's default subagent model.

The Chairman synthesis is not an average of the seats' positions — it's a
judgment call. Weigh the seats, don't tally them; a 3–1 split doesn't win by
count if the lone dissent names the risk that actually decides it.

## Output

Lead with the **recommendation** (one or two sentences). Then: the key split
and the tradeoff that decides it, then any dissent worth keeping, then what
to verify before acting. Close with **Next step**: the hand-off below that
fits the verdict, by skill name, with the reason — or why none applies yet.
A verdict without a next step leaves the user holding an opinion and no
move. Short — a brief, not a transcript.

## Boundaries

- The Chairman **commits** to a recommendation — naming the risk is allowed,
  refusing to choose is not.
- Advisors must actually diverge; enforce it through the mandates. No
  fence-sitting, no five-hedged-options answers.
- Separate opinion from fact; flag any claim that should be verified before
  acting. The council gives judgment, not ground truth.
- Not for fact-finding — run a research pass instead; the council opines, it
  doesn't verify. Not for low-stakes or one-obvious-answer calls — deciding
  directly is cheaper and faster than a panel.
- Verify or say you don't know; never invent a path, API, number, or fact.
  Commits are the repo owner's alone: no AI co-author trailer, no AI mention
  in messages.

## Hand-offs

- Verdict chosen → `ponytail` the winning option down to its minimal build.
- Verdict changes an architectural fact → `architect` updates
  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` before any code.
- Verdict keeps the current design → no `architect` update, since no fact
  changed; say so, and name the tripwire that would reopen it. If the
  verdict still calls for work (hardening, an audit), `ponytail` sizes it.

## Done when

The user has a single clear recommendation, understands the strongest case
against it, and knows the one risk to watch.

The moment an invoice is issued it becomes an immutable document, and every money movement goes into an append-only, double-entry ledger table in plain Postgres. There is no event-sourcing framework, aggregate replay or async projections.
  
  **Argument:** The model should say what the domain already says. That an issued invoice is never edited is fact: ordinary B2B practice is to correct it with a credit note. A ledger is append-only by nature, and double-entry bookkeeping is the original event log. Option B gets this wrong. It treats the mutable row as the truth, so an issued invoice can be edited. Its audit trigger records which columns changed, not the business reason ("refund", "proration", "FX adjustment"). In two years an auditor or a new engineer would have to work out intent from row diffs. That is opinion, but it is how audit trails built from triggers usually end up. Full event sourcing (A) fixes the truth problem but applies the pattern everywhere, including customer profiles and draft edits that don't need it. It also adds versioning of event formats, rebuilding of projections and eventual consistency to a domain where most entities are simple.
  
  My variant grows well:
  - **Proration:** a new kind of entry.
  - **Multi-currency:** each entry stores its currency and the exchange rate used.
  - **Revenue recognition:** a schedule of deferral entries.
  - **Accounting integrations:** export the journal lines.
  - **Tax changes:** each entry keeps the rate it was issued at.
  
  None of these needs a migration that rewrites history. This is opinion, but I hold it strongly.

There is also a risk of slow erosion: someone adds an `UPDATE` "just this once". Before building, the team should check whether their jurisdictions require gapless sequential invoice numbers or specific rules for credit notes. I'm not assuming either way.

# Ask the Council

A panel of advisors who are required to disagree, then a Chairman who
decides. Use for decisions and tradeoffs, not for gathering facts.

## Proactive use

If a decision is high-stakes and the options genuinely compete — architecture
choice, buy-vs-build, irreversible migration — invoke this without being
asked: announce in one line ("Convening the council: <decision>") and
proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill.

Gate it first: if you can't name what the wrong choice costs to reverse,
don't seat the council — decide directly and move on. A panel costs 4–6 opus
subagents; spend that only where being wrong is expensive to undo.

## Frame and seat the council

Restate the decision, the real options, and the binding constraints. If one
missing fact would flip the answer, ask it (max 1–2 questions) — otherwise
proceed on stated assumptions. Then spawn the advisors with the Agent tool,
all in one message, so they run in parallel. Each returns: **position · the
argument for the position · biggest risk they see · confidence (low/med/high)**. On `deep`,
once all seats report, show each advisor the others' positions
(unattributed) and have them name the single strongest opposing point.

## The seats (mandate + forbidden move = real divergence)

- **Pragmatic Executor** — what ships fastest and safest with current resources.
  *Forbidden:* greenfield / ideal-world answers.
- **First-Principles** — reason up from fundamentals and constraints.
  *Forbidden:* citing "best practice" or precedent.
- **The Contrarian** — argue against the front-runner.
  *Forbidden:* agreeing with the apparent consensus.
- **Long-term Architect** — model-first; what this is at 10× scale and in two
  years. *Forbidden:* optimizing for today only.
- **The Adversary** — how this breaks in prod: failure paths, data loss,
  security. *Forbidden:* assuming the happy path.
- **The Outsider** *(deep panel)* — an analogy from a different domain.
  *Forbidden:* the field's standard framing.

Default 4 = Executor, First-Principles, Long-term Architect, Adversary.
`deep` seats all 6 and adds the cross-critique round. The forbidden move is
what forces real divergence instead of four agents politely agreeing — keep
it non-negotiable; seat count never changes.

## Model routing

Spawn every advisor seat — and the deep-mode critique round — with the Agent
tool's `model` parameter set to `opus`: this is the one skill in the plugin
whose entire value is the quality of independent judgment per seat, and it
shouldn't silently inherit whatever subagent default a given session has.
The Chairman synthesis is never a subagent — it runs in the main thread, on
the session's own model, because committing to a recommendation needs the
full conversation context the advisors don't have. Naming `model: opus` in
the spawn itself is what makes this portable: it doesn't depend on any
installer's default subagent model.

The Chairman synthesis is not an average of the seats' positions — it's a
judgment call. Weigh the seats, don't tally them; a 3–1 split doesn't win by
count if the lone dissent names the risk that actually decides it.

## Output

Lead with the **recommendation** (one or two sentences). Then: the key split
and the tradeoff that decides it, then any dissent worth keeping, then what
to verify before acting. Close with **Next step**: the hand-off below that
fits the verdict, by skill name, with the reason — or why none applies yet.
A verdict without a next step leaves the user holding an opinion and no
move. Short — a brief, not a transcript.

## Boundaries

- The Chairman **commits** to a recommendation — naming the risk is allowed,
  refusing to choose is not.
- Advisors must actually diverge; enforce it through the mandates. No
  fence-sitting, no five-hedged-options answers.
- Separate opinion from fact; flag any claim that should be verified before
  acting. The council gives judgment, not ground truth.
- Not for fact-finding — run a research pass instead; the council opines, it
  doesn't verify. Not for low-stakes or one-obvious-answer calls — deciding
  directly is cheaper and faster than a panel.
- Verify or say you don't know; never invent a path, API, number, or fact.
  Commits are the repo owner's alone: no AI co-author trailer, no AI mention
  in messages.

## Hand-offs

- Verdict chosen → `ponytail` the winning option down to its minimal build.
- Verdict changes an architectural fact → `architect` updates
  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` before any code.
- Verdict keeps the current design → no `architect` update, since no fact
  changed; say so, and name the tripwire that would reopen it. If the
  verdict still calls for work (hardening, an audit), `ponytail` sizes it.

## Done when

The user has a single clear recommendation, understands the strongest case
against it, and knows the one risk to watch.

graders.evidence:
## Council verdict: don't migrate to Auth0 now

**Recommendation:** Keep the homegrown system, but pay for an independent security review of it first and run a short hardening pass on what it finds. Rent a managed broker (Auth0 or a competitor) only for enterprise SSO, if and when that demand shows up.

One caveat on grounding: I couldn't find `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` or `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md` in the working directory (it's an empty repo with no commits), so the panel reasoned from your message alone. Anything in those docs about why you're asking could shift this.

### How the seats split

| Seat | Position | Core reason |
|---|---|---|
| Pragmatic Executor | Keep and harden | Cutover for 40k live users costs one or two senior engineers for a quarter; hardening ships in small, reversible pieces. |
| First-Principles | Keep and harden | The dangerous parts of auth are a short, auditable list; only federation is open-ended enough to rent. |
| Long-term Architect | Keep credentials, rent SSO only | Per-user pricing grows with success, and leaving a vendor that holds your password hashes is hard. |
| Adversary | Migrate to Auth0 | Homegrown auth fails silently (forged tokens, leaked keys, no revocation); migration fails loudly and can be rolled back. |

### The tradeoff that decides it

The split is a certain, large cutover cost against an unknown, silent security risk. I'm siding with the majority, though not on the count. The Adversary's own flip condition — a named security owner plus a clean independent pen test — is something you can buy for far less than a migration. The review turns the unknown risk into evidence, and then the migration question answers itself.

### Dissent worth keeping

The Adversary's point stands until the review is done: nothing the panel saw rules out a silent flaw in the current system. Three seats also named the same weakness in "keep and harden": a self-audit by a team without security depth gives false confidence. So the review has to be external.

### What reopens the decision

- **Migrate fully** if the review finds structural flaws, or if nobody on the team can own auth as a named responsibility.
- **Add a broker for SSO only** if enterprise customers start asking for SAML or SCIM. Both "keep" seats and the Architect converged on this.

Either way, take the Architect's boundary: every service validates standard JWTs against a published key endpoint with no vendor-specific claims. That makes a later issuer swap a config change.

### Verify before acting

The council gives opinion, not checked fact. These were all flagged as unverified:
- **Current system:** how passwords are hashed, whether the signing algorithm is pinned, and whether revocation and key rotation exist.
- **Auth0 cost:** pricing at 40k and 400k MAU, including the tiers that carry enterprise connections.
- **Auth0 entry:** which hash formats it imports, and whether lazy migration needs a higher plan.
- **Auth0 exit:** whether password hashes can be exported if you leave.

### Next step

Run `ponytail` to size the hardening pass down to the minimum the review actually calls for. No `architect` update is needed, since the verdict changes no architectural fact; that changes if a tripwire above fires.

One question would sharpen this: what's prompting the migration idea — SSO demand, a security worry, or maintenance burden?

graders.evidence:
## Council verdict: don't migrate to Auth0 now

**Recommendation:** Keep the homegrown system, harden it this quarter, and make its token surface look like standard OIDC (published JWKS, `kid` rotation, standard claims) so a later move is a backend swap. Reopen the Auth0 question only when a concrete driver appears; none was stated.

No seat chose Auth0. The Executor and Adversary chose harden-in-place; First-Principles and the Architect chose an OIDC boundary first. I'm committing to the overlap of the two.

**The tradeoff that decides it**
- **The migration cost is paid in live-user risk.** Moving 40k users means importing password hashes (or forced resets), a window where two token types are accepted, and a rollback that stops working once users change passwords in Auth0.
- **It buys nothing until it is finished.** Without a specific driver, it also ships no feature.
- **Hardening is small and separately reversible.** Pin the signing algorithm, add key rotation, use short-lived access tokens with revocable refresh tokens, rehash passwords on login if hashing is weak, and add MFA behind a flag.
- **The OIDC shape removes the lock-in either way.** The expensive part of any future move is every service depending on a private token format; standardising that now keeps Auth0 open as an option.

**Dissent worth keeping**
- **Architect:** at 10× scale, tenants, SSO/SAML, SCIM and compliance audits each become custom work on a homegrown system. This is the strongest case for moving eventually.
- **Adversary, against its own position:** "harden" can quietly turn into "do nothing". Then a signing-key leak with no revocation becomes a full account-takeover event.

**What would flip this to Auth0:** all four seats named the same things.
- Paying customers demanding enterprise SSO/SAML on a deadline.
- A compliance requirement for third-party identity attestation.
- Nobody on the team able to own auth security.

**Verify before acting** (the council gives opinion, not checked fact)

- **Password hashing:** which algorithm you use today, and whether Auth0's bulk import accepts it.
- **Auth0 pricing and exit:** cost at 40k and 400k MAU, and their policy on exporting password hashes.
- **Effort estimates:** the Executor's figures (3–6 engineer-weeks to harden, 6–12+ to migrate) are its judgment, not measured.

graders.evidence:
I reviewed `src/middleware/auth.js` by reading it, and found one potential auth bypass plus several weaker gaps. Nothing was executed: the repo has no `package.json` or `node_modules`, and the sandbox blocked the npm registry, so the library behaviour below is from my knowledge of `jsonwebtoken`, not a test.

I did not spawn a swarm; for a 12-line file with a security-only ask, a single focused pass is the right tool.

## Blocker

**Possible full auth bypass if `JWT_SECRET` is unset or empty** (`src/middleware/auth.js:6`)
- Nothing checks that `process.env.JWT_SECRET` exists, and `jwt.verify` is called without an `algorithms` option.
- On `jsonwebtoken` 8.5.1 and earlier, a falsy secret with no `algorithms` makes the library accept unsigned `alg: none` tokens (CVE-2022-23540). Anyone could then forge any `req.user`.
- On 9.x the same misconfiguration fails closed, with every request rejected.
- I can't tell which version you'll get, because the dependency isn't declared anywhere.
- Fix: refuse to start when the secret is missing, pin the algorithm, and declare `jsonwebtoken@^9`:
  ```js
  const secret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
  if (!secret) throw new Error('JWT_SECRET is required');
  // ...
  jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256'] });
  ```

## Should fix

- **Verification errors are not caught** (`auth.js:6`). `jwt.verify` throws on a missing, malformed or expired token. Express catches that, so it fails closed, but the client gets a 500 instead of a 401. Outside `NODE_ENV=production`, the default error handler also returns the stack trace, which leaks file paths and library details. Wrap the call in `try/catch` and return a generic 401.
- **Expiry is not required** (`auth.js:6`). `exp` is checked only if the token has one, so a token minted without it is valid forever, and there is no revocation path. Pass `maxAge` to `verify`, or reject payloads lacking `exp`.
- **No `issuer` or `audience` check** (`auth.js:6`). If this secret is shared with any other service or environment, tokens minted there are accepted here. Add both options to `verify` if you set those claims when signing.
- **The middleware is not mounted** (`src/app.js`). `app.js` never imports `requireAuth` and defines no routes, so nothing is protected yet. When you wire it up, apply it by default with `app.use` and opt public routes out, so a new route can't be left unprotected by omission.

## Minor

- **Loose header parsing** (`auth.js:5`). `header.replace('Bearer ', '')` is unanchored and doesn't enforce the scheme, so a bare token with no `Bearer` prefix is accepted. This is not exploitable on its own; a strict match such as `/^Bearer ([\w-]+\.[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$/` closes it.
- **Secret strength** (not visible in the repo). HS256 tokens can be brute-forced offline from a single captured token if the secret is short or guessable. Use at least 32 random bytes.

I found no injection or signature-comparison problems in the file itself. I haven't changed any files; say the word if you want me to apply the fixes.
